intro.title: Como funciona
intro.subtitle: Medir é entender comportamento. Os eventos mostram como as pessoas usam cada parte da interface, e é com esses dados que o time decide o que melhorar. O sistema resolve a parte difícil: todos os eventos seguem a mesma convenção de nomes e o mesmo formato de dados — relatórios de produtos diferentes falam a mesma língua.
intro.body: Dois princípios definem o desenho. Primeiro: o evento não vive dentro do componente — um botão do sistema não rastreia nada sozinho. O rastreamento é inserido quando o componente é usado na construção da página, com o contexto que só o produto conhece (qual botão, em qual tela, para qual ação). Segundo: a coleta pode ser automatizada — a skill /analytics instrumenta páginas inteiras seguindo os padrões definidos aqui, sem chamadas manuais espalhadas pelo código.
intro.audience: Esta página serve a quem instrumenta páginas de produto, a quem documenta componentes e a quem analisa os dados no GA4.
intro.note: Detalhe técnico da documentação: o GA4 carrega uma única vez no manager do Storybook (manager-head.html, com send_page_view: false); as páginas chamam track(evento, dados), que envia via window.top.gtag — sem isso, todo evento seria atribuído a /iframe.html.

intro.title: How it works
intro.subtitle: Measuring is understanding behavior. Events show how people use each part of the interface, and that data is what the team uses to decide what to improve. The system solves the hard part: every event follows the same naming convention and the same data shape — reports from different products speak the same language.
intro.body: Two principles define the design. First: the event does not live inside the component — a system button tracks nothing by itself. Tracking is inserted when the component is used to build the page, with context only the product knows (which button, on which screen, for which action). Second: collection can be automated — the /analytics skill instruments whole pages following the standards defined here, without manual calls scattered through the code.
intro.audience: This page serves whoever instruments product pages, whoever documents components, and whoever analyzes the data in GA4.
intro.note: Documentation technical detail: GA4 loads once in the Storybook manager (manager-head.html, with send_page_view: false); pages call track(event, data), which sends via window.top.gtag — without it, every event would be attributed to /iframe.html.

naming.title: Naming convention
naming.subtitle: Format [object]_[action], always in English, snake_case, past-tense verb, maximum 3 words.

rules.language: Always English — never pt-BR or es.
rules.case: snake_case — never camelCase, PascalCase or kebab-case.
rules.tense: Action in the short verb form (click, open, change, select) — consistent with the typed catalog. Never gerunds (clicking) or long infinitives (to_submit).

payload.title: Base payload
payload.subtitle: Every track() call must include the three global properties. Component-specific properties are added as needed.

location.desc: Page or section where the component sits (header, checkout_form).

docsEvents.title: Universal docs page events
docsEvents.subtitle: Fired by every docs page — no manual instrumentation needed. Payloads follow the typed catalog in src/lib/analytics.ts.

sectionViewed.fire: After 2s of continuous visibility of a section. Suppresses false positives during programmatic scroll.

nav.fire: Click on a doc sidebar navigation item.

link.fire: Click on a generic tracked link.

componentEvents.title: Per-component catalog
componentEvents.subtitle: Expected events for the most common components. The docs page (or consuming product) calls track() — the primitive never does.

navClick.when: When a nav item is clicked.

fieldChange.component: Checkbox, Switch, Select, RadioGroup, Slider, Calendar, Toggle

commandSelect.when: When a list item is selected.

items.inPrimitive: Never call track() inside a UI primitive. Tracking is the product layer's job (docs page or feature).
items.sensitive: Don't track sensitive data: email, national ID, phone, internal IDs, raw search query. Use query_length or has_value.
items.nonEnglish: No Portuguese names or camelCase. The auditor fails on botaoClicado.
items.directGtag: Never call gtag() directly. Always via track() — it guarantees window.top and sanitization.

privacy.title: Privacy and fallback
privacy.subtitle: Measuring is desirable, but never a condition for the interface to work — and whoever blocks measurement is not penalized for it.

items.blocked: Not every visit produces data: ad blockers, test environments and privacy-protecting browsers prevent measurement from loading — and that is expected. When it happens, track() simply does nothing: the page keeps working, no error appears.
items.noBuffer: Nothing is stored in the browser for later sending: if measurement was not active at the moment of the interaction, that data does not exist.
items.noSensitive: We do not collect sensitive data: no emails, names or content typed into fields. Events describe interactions — which component, which variant, in which part of the screen — not people.
